summary.value: The Castellana Negra is an old Spanish laying breed, often linked to the Moorish period, when it was called the moruna. It was once the common farm hen of central and southern Spain, then nearly vanished when caged hybrid layers took over. Conservation flocks built from a handful of birds in the 1980s brought it back, and about 2,200 were counted in 2024, still a vulnerable number. It is a light, Mediterranean type bird dressed in solid black with a green sheen, a red single comb with five or six points, white earlobes and dark slate legs. Roosters weigh about 6 to 6.5 pounds and hens about 5 pounds. Hens start laying at four to five months and give around 200 to 225 large white eggs a year. They are hardy, resist disease well and seldom go broody.
